title: Australian Small Business and Family Enterprise Ombudsman (Consequential and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2015
short_title: Australian Small Business and Family Enterprise Ombudsman (Consequential and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2015

speeches.speaker: Bruce Billson
speeches.brief: The Australian Small Business and Family Enterprise Ombudsman Bill 2015 was moved to establish a statutory ombudsman to advocate for and assist small businesses and family enterprises, citing over 2 million small businesses (96% of all businesses) producing $330 billion and employing 4.5 million people, while criticising the former Labor government for losing 519,000 small business jobs and reducing the small business workforce share from 52% to 43%.

speeches.speaker: Bruce Billson
speeches.brief: The Australian Small Business and Family Enterprise Ombudsman (Consequential and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2015 amends the Commonwealth Ombudsman Act 1976 to allow the Commonwealth Ombudsman to transfer matters to the new Ombudsman, and transfers ongoing work from the Australian Small Business Commissioner to the Ombudsman upon its creation.

speeches.speaker: Bernie Ripoll
speeches.brief: Labor supported the Australian Small Business and Family Enterprise Ombudsman Bill 2015 but raised concerns that sections 67(2)(b), 67(2)(c) and 69(1) could limit the Ombudsman’s independence and impartiality, particularly in disputes between small businesses and government agencies. The speaker also noted that the bill’s provisions on termination of appointment lacked a statutory immunity clause and that the Ombudsman’s powers to hold hearings required ministerial referral.

speeches.speaker: Gai Brodtmann
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the two bills establishing the Australian Small Business and Family Enterprise Ombudsman, noting Labor's previous initiatives such as the Australian Small Business Commissioner (Mark Brennan) and the National Business Names Registry, while urging the new Ombudsman to address government procurement problems including lengthy contracts, high insurance costs, and tender processes that disadvantage small and micro businesses.

speeches.speaker: Karen Andrews
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the Australian Small Business and Family Enterprise Ombudsman Bill 2015, arguing it fulfills a 2013 election commitment to streamline dispute resolution and cut red tape, citing $2.4 billion in savings. The Ombudsman will serve as an advocate and concierge for dispute resolution, avoiding duplication of existing services, and the speaker noted over 2 million small businesses in Australia, with 96% of all businesses being small.

speeches.speaker: Michelle Landry
speeches.brief: The speaker announced the Australian Small Business and Family Enterprise Ombudsman Bill 2015 and its consequential provisions bill, which establish a new ombudsman to advocate for, assist, and mediate disputes for small businesses. The speech also highlighted the $5.5 billion Growing Jobs and Small Business package, including a $20,000 instant asset write-off and a company tax rate cut to 28.5 per cent for businesses with turnover under $2 million, with the ombudsman expected to deliver net savings of $18.395 million per year.

speeches.speaker: Bruce Billson
speeches.brief: The Australian Small Business and Family Enterprise Ombudsman Bill 2015 establishes a statutory ombudsman appointed by the Governor-General, with advocacy and assistance functions including early dispute resolution and referral of matters to other agencies. The government confirmed the ombudsman will not make binding decisions, and the opposition indicated its support for the bills.
